requirement: R26 Transport/SSE B5 first slice (AbortSignal to I/O, scoped cleanup, typed failures, exact per-operation retry). SSE frame semantics untouched.

changedFiles.role-model-router/apps/runtime-host-brid: privateRetentionRequest now accepts/forwards an AbortSignal, has scoped response-reader/listener cleanup, adds typed abort/protocol failures, and exposes an Effect.tryPromise wrapper; retry schedule preserved

changed: track-b-operations.ts privateRetentionRequest fetch call: (options.fetchImpl ?? fetch)(url, { ...requestInit, signal: requestSignal }), where requestSignal = AbortSignal.any([callerSignal, AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs)]) (caller signal omitted only when absent).
track-b-operations.ts requestPrivate wrapper now accepts an optional AbortSignal (4th argument) and passes it into privateRetentionRequest.

track-b-operations.ts new privateRetentionRequestEffect: Effect.tryPromise with a (signal) thunk (arity rule: internal/effect.ts:1166; notes line 27) forwarding the fiber signal into privateRetentionRequest.
verifiedUnchanged: index.ts:28084-28106 provider HTTP call already forwards executionOptions?.requestOptions?.abortSignal to networkFetcher; this slice did not need to change it.

SSE frame semantics untouched: readCodexResponsesSseTranscript (index.ts:13503-13568), readProviderStreamTranscript, chunk/DONE/error handling were not modified. The new reader is the private-operation JSON body reader, not the SSE parser.

abortProof.test: cancels the underlying fetch when the enclosing fiber times out (request does not keep running)
abortProof.setup: fetchImpl returns a promise that settles only on the AbortSignal it receives; privateRetentionRequestEffect is run under Effect.timeout(..., '30 millis').
assertions: the fetch stub observed abort (state.aborted true) - the request did not keep running after the fiber was interrupted

scopedCleanup.implementation: one AbortSignal listener on the caller signal removed in finally; one response.body reader acquired per response, cancelled on read failure/abort and lock-released in finally; both releases reported through the injectable onRelease hook.

counts.statusFailurePath: onRelease = ['abort-listener', 'reader'] (status 500 after a successful fetch body read)
counts.callerAbortPath: onRelease = ['abort-listener', 'reader'] (abort during body read cancels the reader, then releases the lock/listener)

scopedCleanup.test: counts scoped releases on the status-failure path; counts scoped releases on the caller-abort path and does not retry

new.name: TrackBPrivateOperationAbortError
new.when: caller signal already aborted, or aborted during fetch/body read; terminal, never retried

new.name: TrackBPrivateOperationProtocolError
new.when: 2xx response body is not valid JSON; terminal, never retried

preserved.name: TrackBPrivateOperationTimeoutError
preserved.note: still the timeout identity; status 504/message unchanged

preserved.name: TrackBPrivateOperationError
preserved.note: stated status failures keep their class/status/message (504 or the HTTP status)

typedFailures.nuance: A non-2xx body that is not JSON keeps the old lenient {} fallback so a stated status still surfaces as TrackBPrivateOperationError with its status (no new protocol class for status failures).

red.mutation: pre-aborted caller signal throws a generic Error
red.message: expected Error: aborted to be an instance of TrackBPrivateOperationAbortError

retrySchedule.behaviour: 5 fetch attempts on a retryable connection-level failure, sleeps exactly 250/1000/2500/5000ms (existing schedule preserved, now pinned in the new suite as well as the existing run100m test).
noRetry: caller abort (pre-aborted or during I/O): zero fetch retries
protocol violation: one fetch, no retry
status failure: one fetch, no retry

sseUntouched: This slice does not change tool/reasoning/fragmentation/drain/first-substantive/DONE/error frame semantics or any SSE parser/reader; it only handles the private-operation JSON response. No queue changes either.

typecheck.note: host tsconfig excludes test/**, so it typechecks the source change; the new test is transformed by Vitest.
